references.author: Parco archeologico del Colosseo
references.observation: The visitor route inaugurated in December 2024 enters the western sector through Gallery XXIV and ends at the Octagonal Hall. The eastern access intervention has a separate approach.

references.author: Parco archeologico del Colosseo
references.observation: The 1:500 plan locates the west gallery, perimeter corridor 92, Octagonal Hall 128 and five radial rooms. The visitor route drawing shows their broad relationship. The model derives relative positions from these plans.

references.author: Soprintendenza per i beni archeologici di Roma
references.observation: The numbered tour map begins at Gallery XXIV, passes the western painted rooms and pentagonal court, connects to corridor 92 and reaches the octagonal complex through the rooms along the west edge. It records the route topology used in the model.

references.author: Parco archeologico del Colosseo
references.observation: The Octagonal Hall's lintels are about 4.34 m high and span 3.45–3.86 m. The lower vault follows the eight sides, and the upper vault closes around a 5.92 m circular oculus.
The surviving dome is exposed masonry. A translucent modern cover is visible inside the oculus.
The z15 extract identifies the site and surrounding Viale Serapide and Viale della Domus Aurea. Its Domus Aurea POI is a site reference. No buried room outline is available in the extract.

references.author: Acaia 61 Studio Architecture
references.observation: The architect’s photographs document the 2024 lower brick arch and dark upper shutter, an open gray entrance leaf, the stair with solid side panels, two lit filaments above surviving column bases, and the adjacent rough Roman wall. The new stair has a single freestanding steel flight descending into Gallery XXIV. The exterior arch and stair are modeled from photo proportions.

references.author: Esri and contributors
references.observation: Public aerial imagery independently shows the western curved terrace, smaller neighboring ruin and path terminus present in the retained PMTiles. Imagery is reference only.

limitation: The underground route and retaining wall use a plan registered to the surface. The stair and terrace elevations use photographic proportions and the standard terrain.
researchPointNote: The point identifies the general archaeological site. The authored origin and signed orientation are in map-frame.json.
